The book walkthrough: one command, then Excel

What the firm asked for, 14 Oct 2026: "i want you to make it work so i can generate this workbook at work with the script, it should be debugged and walked through and tied out."

This is the walk: the workbook built the way it is built at work, then used in Excel 16 the way a person uses it (clicking the buttons, typing in the yellow row, saving, closing and opening it again), and every answer read back from Excel and set beside an answer written down beforehand from the source files.

1. Build

From threshold-engine/:

python -m threshold_engine peers pull --cache books/ind_cache --first 2006Q1 --last 2026Q2 --products "Credit card" Mortgage "Home equity" "Other consumer" Auto --delinquency yes --mergers 2005-01-01
python -m threshold_engine book books/consumer-public.json consumer-credit.xlsx

The walkthrough ran the second command on a copy of the book whose only change is where the cache is (prepare.py): the cache pulled on 14 Oct 2026 was used rather than pulled again. Expected: Wrote consumer-credit.xlsx: 105 series, 82 quarters; open it on Summary, decide on Decide. It took 8 min 48 s on the last run (12 min 42 s on the first), almost all of it the peers build reading the cache.

2. The steps

The steps are cumulative, as a session is: what is typed in one step is still there in the next.

One set of lines per product and measure (the firm, 15 Oct 2026: "we don't need to set thresholds on all 3, we need to use all 3 to set appropriate thresholds"): Decide has 35 rows, and each row's Lines set from picks the source whose history sets its lines.

Step What you do What it shows
B1 Open the workbook It opens on Summary; the tabs in order (Assess, Chart and Peers workings hidden); two slicers, one button each; Decide shows the first product and measure, no source picked, nothing decided; no links, no errors
B2 Read Summary and Lines by source All 105 series' latest value, Pick a source where each rating goes, and every series' own lines equal the reference
B3 On Decide, click Credit card and Nonaccrual, and pick KeyBank under Lines set from One row; the lines are KeyBank's own; every source rated on them, beside what its own history would give; Thresholds holds the same
B4 Type 3.5 under How rare High is (z) High's line moves for every source of the row; Thresholds and Summary follow
B5 Leave out 2012Q3 to 2013Q4, the period Decide suggests, with a reason KeyBank's lines move as the reference says, the industry's own lines do not; Assess lists the period under KeyBank's series, whole
B6, B6b Clear the reason; type it back Refused, in words, on Decide and Thresholds; then the lines as in B5
B7 Accept these lines, with a note Decided: 1 of 35; the decision on Thresholds, and on Lines by source beside KeyBank only
B8 Click Auto and Net charge-offs, and pick Industry (every bank) KeyBank's life-to-date history rated on the lines the industry's longer history gives
B9 Click Mortgage and Net charge-offs, and pick Industry (every bank) Refused, with the number that would fix it
B10 Save, close, open again Every pick, decision and setting still there, and the lines with them

A step passes when every cell it reads says what steps.json says: a number within 1e-9, text exactly.

3. How it was run

python docs/walkthrough-book/prepare.py PATH-TO-CACHE
python -m threshold_engine book docs/walkthrough-book/out/book.json docs/walkthrough-book/out/consumer-credit.xlsx
python docs/walkthrough-book/expected.py docs/walkthrough-book/out/book.json
copy docs\walkthrough-book\out\consumer-credit.xlsx docs\walkthrough-book\out\walk.xlsx
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File docs\walkthrough-book\walk.ps1
python docs/walkthrough-book/compare.py

expected.py writes the answers from the series CSVs and scale.py, never from the workbook. walk.ps1 does each step in Excel through Excel's own automation and reads each answer back. compare.py writes RESULT.md.

And, separately, that the file opens without Excel repairing it:

powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\check_slicers_in_excel.ps1 -Path docs\walkthrough-book\out\consumer-credit.xlsx -Sheet Decide -Table Decisions -Shapes 3 -Expect "Slicer_Product=Credit card|Slicer_Measure=Net charge-offs" -SwitchCache Slicer_Measure -SwitchTo "Gross charge-offs"

"No errors" in B1 means none a reader can see: on the visible tabs, outside hidden rows and columns. The rest are counted by kind and are all #N/A, the gap a chart leaves where a quarter has no value (on the run of 15 Oct 2026: Assess 169, Chart 8,470, Decide 249, Peers workings 1,556).

4. What it does not prove

  • The peer tabs are counted for errors and links (B1) but their numbers are not checked against a reference here; tests/test_peers*.py hold them.
  • One series is tied to the filing (../tie-out/keybank-card-nonaccrual-2026-10-14/); the other 104 rest on the same code and the reference, not on a filing each.
  • Three of the 35 rows have a source picked in the walk (Credit card nonaccrual, Auto and Mortgage net charge-offs); the other 32 are read blank (Pick a source) on Summary, and every source's own lines are read for all 105 on Lines by source.
  • Thresholds' latest value is written by the build, not a live formula on Data: pasting a corrected quarter into Data moves the lines but not the latest value (found by the tie-out).
